memoryText: The LORD was with Joseph, and whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. The week you have completed followed Joseph from his lowest point, sold into slavery, falsely accused, forgotten in prison, to his elevation as second over Egypt. Take time today to consider how God was with Joseph at every stage of his descent.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Genesis 39:23 is the refrain of the Joseph story. The phrase “The LORD was with Joseph” appears multiple times, when he is sold as a slave, when he is in Potiphar’s house, when he is in prison, when he stands before Pharaoh. Wherever he is, the LORD is with him.

This is the gospel’s promise restated. Joseph’s circumstances ranged from privileged son to abused slave to wrongly accused prisoner to ruler of Egypt. In every condition, the LORD was with him. The presence of God was not contingent on Joseph’s success. It was the source of his eventual success, but it was equally present in his lowest moments.

Say the verse to yourself, particularly the second half, “whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed.” This is not a promise that everything you attempt will work out. It is a promise that God’s purposes through you cannot fail. Joseph’s “success” included thirteen years of suffering. The LORD’s success and our preferred outcomes are not always the same thing, but they are always good, and they are always sure.
weekInReview:
The week began with Esau’s genealogy and then plunged into the Joseph story, the dreams, the brothers’ hatred, the selling into slavery. You read the strange Judah-Tamar story alongside Joseph’s integrity in Potiphar’s house. You worshiped through both halves of Psalm 37, learning the wisdom of patience while the wicked seem to prosper. You watched Joseph rise from prison to second in command over all of Egypt. And the week ended with his brothers standing before him without recognizing him, bowing down, just as Joseph’s childhood dreams had foretold.

The week is about hidden providence. Joseph could not see what God was doing. The brothers could not see what God was undoing. But the LORD was with Joseph at every step, through betrayal, false accusation, forgotten years in prison, and the same LORD was preparing the moment of reversal.
reflectionQuestions: Where in your life right now does it feel like the LORD is not “making it succeed”? Joseph’s experience suggests that God’s presence is not always evident through circumstances. The thirteen years between Joseph’s sale and his elevation included times when even he must have wondered if God had forgotten him. What season are you in? How does Joseph’s story help you wait?

How does Joseph point you to Christ? Joseph was the beloved son, sold for silver, falsely accused, imprisoned with criminals, elevated to a throne, and used by God to save the very brothers who had betrayed him. Every detail prefigures Jesus. Where do you see Christ most clearly in the Joseph story? And how does seeing Joseph’s reversal deepen your hope in Christ’s resurrection?

Where do you need to choose integrity in your own “Potiphar’s house”? Joseph said no to a powerful person’s advances when no one would have known. He chose the harder right over the easier wrong. Is there a place in your life today where integrity will cost you something? What would it look like to choose it anyway, trusting that the LORD is with you?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for being with Joseph in the pit, in prison, and on the throne, and for being with you in every season.
Ask him to make you a person of integrity in the place you are right now.
Rest in his presence this Sabbath, in success and in failure.
